content:
maya: starting gaia-edge1 bring-up, gpu-run1 nodepool failed validation during post-provision checks. seeing NotReady nodes and IPAM allocation mismatch. anyone able to take a look?

sam: on it. brief details? which subnet/prefix did the terraform create vs IPAM?

maya: terraform created 10.240.32.0/22 for worker pools but IPAM expected 10.240.128.0/22. new subnet overlapped reserved control plane range.

igor: that explains kubelet bootstrap failures. nodes pick IPs but API server cert SANs don't match the cluster-cidr mapping. "kubectl get nodes" shows `NetworkUnavailable` and `NotReady` with kubelet complaining about cni config.

maya: also seeing this in node logs: 
```
Mar 22 12:16:04 worker-3 kubelet[1234]: E0322 12:16:04.123456 kubelet.go:243] Failed to set cni config: failed to reserve IP from IPAM pool: allocation conflict
Mar 22 12:16:04 worker-3 kubelet[1234]: E0322 12:16:04.123460 kubelet.go:451] Node registration failed: san mismatch: expected 10.240.128.0/22
```

deploy-bot: :warning: Auto-rollback triggered for rollout/gpu-run1 (policy: validation-failure). Rolled back to previous stable pool config.

sam: rollback succeeded but we still need a clean plan to re-provision without stomping the reserved ranges. don't want repeat.

ops-sre: quick checklist: 1) freeze new subnet allocation in terraform 2) sync with ipam team to reserve 10.240.32.0/22 or pick a new /22 3) re-run cluster validation locally with `./tools/validate-cluster --cidr=...` 4) DRY-RUN apply via staging account

maya: yep. ipam pinged, they already reserved 10.240.128.0/22 for control-plane. they can either hand over 10.240.32.0/22 or we pick 10.240.64.0/22. any preference?

igor: prefer 10.240.64.0/22 to keep control-plane and workers farther apart. fewer blast radius interactions.

sam: agreed. I'll update terraform var `worker_cidr` to 10.240.64.0/22 and run `terraform plan -var=worker_cidr=10.240.64.0/22`.

maya: note: when we reprovision we hit a second issue last run — journal shows `nvidia-persistenced failed to start` on some nodes and driver mismatch between kernel module and installed driver package. suspect AMI drift. pls validate AMI image tag.

igor: good catch. AMI used by previous stable pool: `redwood-gpu-ami:v3.9` but the new rollout referenced `redwood-gpu-ami:v3.11` which has a newer driver that needs kernel 6.x. our kernels are 5.15 LTS. either update node kernel or pin ami to v3.9 for now.

anya: taking handoff. plan: (1) lock terraform changes in PR and request reviewer (sam/igor) (2) update worker_cidr to 10.240.64.0/22 and run `terraform apply --target=module.subnet` in staging, (3) verify IPAM allocation with netops (confirm reservation), (4) pin AMI to v3.9 and run a canary of 3 nodes, (5) run cluster validation script and smoke tests, (6) escalate to infra-oncall if canary nodes fail to join.

maya: +1. timeline? we should avoid another big rollback during business hours.

anya: will do canary now in staging, if green promote to prod after 30m. I'll post updates here.

sam: if canary fails due to driver, we can launch a quick job to `apt-get` the correct kernel headers and reboot, but prefer pinning AMI.

maya: cost note — switching AMI version may change baseline GPU driver performance; if we stick to v3.9 we might lose some perf gains in v3.11 but that's acceptable to get stable nodes. log perf impact for Optimize team.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary rollout completed (3/3 nodes ready) in staging for pool/gpu-run1.

anya: staging smoke passes. proceeding to prod apply window at 02:30 UTC. ops-sre please standby for monitoring and fast rollback if latency/error budgets spike.

ops-sre: standing by. will watch node join events and infra metrics (packet drops, ipam allocation errors, kernel OOM). will also have a rollback snapshot ready.

maya: handing off fully to anya for prod apply. thanks everyone.

anya: taking over — will comment on PR with final runbook steps and link to this thread. ping me if you need the runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/edge-gpu-bootstrap

sam: thx. follow-up: add an automated preflight check to our pipeline that validates requested CIDR against IPAM before apply. reduce leak-of-human-error risk.

igor: agreed. will open a ticket to add CIDR preflight to the provisioner pipeline.

maya: closing loop: recorded action items in #infra-ops board. thanks. :tada:
